2600: from חֵן; gratis, i.e. devoid of cost, reason or advantage; without a cause (cost, wages), causeless, to cost nothing, free(-ly), innocent, for nothing (nought, in vain.
2601: probably by orthographical variation for חֲנַנְאֵל; Chanamel, an Israelite; Hanameel.
2602: of uncertain derivation; perhaps the aphis or plantlouse; frost.
2603: a primitive root (compare חָנָה); properly, to bend or stoop in kindness to an inferior; to favor, bestow; causatively to implore (i.e. move to favor by petition); beseech, [idiom] fair, (be, find, shew) favour(-able), be (deal, give, grant (gracious(-ly), intreat, (be) merciful, have (shew) mercy (on, upon), have pity upon, pray, make supplication, [idiom] very.
2604: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָנַן; to favor or (causatively) to entreat; shew mercy, make supplication.
2605: from חָנַן; favor; Chanan, the name of seven Israelites; Canan.
2606: from חָנַן and אֵל; God has favored; Chananel, probably an Israelite, from whom a tower of Jerusalem was named; Hananeel.
2607: from חָנַן; gracious; Chanani, the name of six Israelites; Hanani.
2608: or חֲנַנְיָהוּ; from חָנַן and יָהּ; Jah has favored; Chananjah, the name of thirteen Israelites; Hananiah.
2609: of Egyptian derivation; Chanes, a place in Egypt; Hanes.
2610: a primitive root; to soil, especially in a moral sense; corrupt, defile, [idiom] greatly, pollute, profane.
2611: from חָנֵף; soiled (i.e. with sin), impious; hypocrite(-ical).
2612: from חָנֵף; moral filth, i.e. wickedness; hypocrisy.
2614: a primitive root (compare חָנַךְ); to be narrow; by implication, to throttle, or (reflex.) to choke oneself to death (by a rope); hang self, strangle.
2615: probably from חָנַן; favored; Channathon, a place in Palestine; Hannathon.
2616: a primitive root; (compare חָנַן); (compare בָרַךְ); properly, perhaps to bow (the neck only in courtesy to an equal), i.e. to be kind; also (by euphemistically, but rarely) to reprove; shew self merciful, put to shame.
2617: from חָסַד; kindness; by implication (towards God) piety; rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty; favour, good deed(-liness, -ness), kindly, (loving-) kindness, merciful (kindness), mercy, pity, reproach, wicked thing.
2618: the same as חֵסֵד; favor; Chesed, an Israelite; Hesed.
2619: from חֵסֵד and יָהּ; Jah has favored; Chasadjah, an Israelite; Hasadiah.
2620: a primitive root; (compare בָּטַח); to flee for protection; figuratively, to confide in; have hope, make refuge, (put) trust.
2621: from חָסָה; hopeful; Chosah, an Israelite; also a place in Palestine; Hosah.
2623: from חָסַד; properly, kind, i.e. (religiously) pious (a saint); godly (man), good, holy (one), merciful, saint, (un-) godly.
2624: feminine of חָסִיד; the kind (maternal) bird, i.e. a stork; [idiom] feather, stork.
2625: from חָסַל; the ravager, i.e. a locust; caterpillar.
2626: from חָסַן; properly, firm, i.e. (by implication) mighty; strong.
2627: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to חָסֵר; deficient; wanting.
2628: a primitive root; to eat off; consume.
2629: a primitive root; to muzzle; by analogy, to stop the nose; muzzle, stop.
2630: a primitive root; properly, to (be) compact; by implication, to hoard; lay up.
2631: (Aramaic) corresponding to חָסַן; to hold in occupancy; possess.
2633: from חָסַן; wealth; riches, strength, treasure.
2635: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of חַסְפַּס; a clod; clay.
2636: reduplicated from an unused root meaning apparently to peel; a shred or scale; round thing.
2637: a primitive root; to lack; by implication, to fail, want, lessen; be abated, bereave, decrease, (cause to) fail, (have) lack, make lower, want.
2638: from חָסֵר; lacking; hence, without; destitute, fail, lack, have need, void, want.
2639: from חָסֵר; lack; hence, destitution; poverty, want.
2640: from חָסֵר; poverty; in want of.
2641: from חָסֵר; want; Chasrah, an Israelite; Hasrah.
2643: from חׇפַף (in the moral sense of covered from soil); pure; innocent.
2644: an orthographical variation of חָפָה; properly, to cover, i.e. (in a sinister sense) to act covertly; do secretly.
2645: a primitive root (compare חָפָא, חׇפַף); to cover; by implication, to veil, to encase, protect; ceil, cover, overlay.
2646: from חָפָה; a canopy; chamber, closet, defence.
2647: the same as חֻפָּה; Chuppah, an Israelite; Huppah.
2648: a primitive root; properly, to start up suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to hasten away, to fear; (make) haste (away), tremble.
2650: plural of חֻפָּה (compare חוּפָם); Chuppim, an Israelite; Huppim.
2651: from an unused root of uncertain signification; a fist (only in the dual); fists, (both) hands, hand(-ful).
2652: from חֹפֶן; perhaps pugilist; Chophni, an Israelite; Hophni.
2653: a primitive root (compare חָפָה, יָחֵף); to cover (in protection); cover.
2654: a primitive root; properly, to incline to; by implication (literally but rarely) to bend; figuratively, to be pleased with, desire; [idiom] any at all, (have, take) delight, desire, favour, like, move, be (well) pleased, have pleasure, will, would.
2655: from חָפֵץ; pleased with; delight in, desire, favour, please, have pleasure, whosoever would, willing, wish.
2656: from חָפֵץ; pleasure; hence (abstractly) desire; concretely, a valuable thing; hence (by extension) a matter (as something in mind); acceptable, delight(-some), desire, things desired, matter, pleasant(-ure), purpose, willingly.
2657: from חֵפֶץ with suffixes; my delight (is) in her; Cheptsi-bah, a fanciful name for Palestine; Hephzi-bah.
2658: a primitive root; properly, to pry into; by implication, to delve, to explore; dig, paw, search out, seek.
2659: a primitive root (perhaps rather the same as חָפַר through the idea of detection); to blush; figuratively, to be ashamed, disappointed; causatively, to shame, reproach; be ashamed, be confounded, be brought to confusion (unto shame), come (be put to) shame, bring reproach.
2660: from חָפַר or חָפֵר; a pit of shame; Chepher, a place in Palestine; also the name of three Israelites; Hepher.
2661: from חָפַר; a hole; only in connection with פֵּרָה, which ought rather to be joined as one word, thus חַפַרְפֵּרָה; by reduplication from חָפַר; a burrower, i.e. probably a rat; [phrase] mole.
2662: patronymically from חֵפֶר; a Chephrite (collectively) or descendants of Chepher; Hepherites.
2663: dual of חֵפֶר; double pit; Chapharajim, a place in Palestine; Haphraim.
2664: a primitive root; to seek; causatively, to conceal oneself (i.e. let be sought), or mask; change, (make) diligent (search), disquise self, hide, search (for, out).
2665: from חָפַשׂ; something covert, i.e. a trick; search.
2666: a primitive root; to spread loose; figuratively, to manumit; be free.
2667: from חָפַשׁ; something spread loosely, i.e. a carpet; precious.
2669: and חׇפְשִׁית; from חָפַשׁ; (with בַּיִת, a hospital); prostration by sickness; several.
2670: from חָפַשׁ; exempt (from bondage, tax or care); free, liberty.
2671: from חָצַץ; also by interchange for עֵץ; properly, a piercer, i.e. an arrow; by implication, a wound; figuratively, (of God) thunderbolt; the shaft of aspear; [phrase] archer, arrow, dart, shaft, staff, wound.
2672: or חָצֵב; a primitive root; to cut or carve (wood, stone or other material); by implication, to hew, split, square, quarry, engrave; cut, dig, divide, grave, hew (out, -er), made, mason.
2673: lemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה; a primitive root (compare זֵד)); to cut or split in two; to halve; divide, [idiom] live out half, reach to the midst, participle
2674: a collective form of חָצֵר; village; Chatsor, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine and of one in Arabia; Hazor.
2675: from חָצוֹר and a Aramaizing form of the feminine of חָדָשׁ (compare חֲדָת); new Chatsor, a place in Palestine; Hazor, Hadattah (as if two places).
2676: lemma חָעוֹת ayin, corrected to חָצוֹת; from חָצָהlemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה; the middle (of the night); mid(-night).
2677: from חָצָהlemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה; the half or middle; half, middle, mid(-night), midst, part, two parts.
2678: or חֵצִי; prolongation from חֵץ; an arrow; arrow.
2679: from חֵצִי and the plural of מְנוּחָה, with the article interposed; midst of the resting-places; Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth, an Israelite; half of the Manahethites.
2680: patronymically from חֲצִי הַמְּנֻחוֹת; a Chatsi-ham-Menachtite or descendant of Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth; half of the Manahethites.
2681: a collateral form of חָצֵר; a court or abode; court.
2682: perhaps originally the same as חָצִיר, from the greenness of a courtyard; grass; also a leek (collectively); grass, hay, herb, leek.
2683: from an unused root meaning to hold firmly; the bosom (as comprised between the arms); bosom.
2684: a collateral form of חֵצֶן, and meaning the same; {the bosom (as comprised between the arms)}; arm, lap.
2685: (Aramaic) a primitive root; properly, to shear or cut close; figuratively, to be severe; hasty, be urgent.
2686: a primitive root (compare חָצָהlemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה); also as denominative from חֵץ; properly, to chop into, pierce or sever; hence, to curtail, to distribute (into ranks); to shoot an arrow; archer, [idiom] bands, cut off in the midst.
2687: from חָצָץ; also like חֵץ; properly, something cutting; hence, gravel (as grit); an arrow; arrow, gravel (stone).
2688: or חַצֲצֹן תָּמָר; from חָצַץ and תָּמָר; division (i.e. perhaps row) of (the) palm-tree; Chatsetson-tamar, a place in Palestine; Hazezon-tamar.
2689: by reduplication from חָצַר; a trumpet (from its sundered or quavering note); trumpet(-er).
2690: a primitive root; properly, to surround with a stockade, and thus separate from the open country; but used only in the reduplicated form חֲצֹצֵר; or (2 Chronicles 5:12) חֲצֹרֵר; as dem. from חֲצֹצְרָה; to trumpet, i.e. blow on that instrument; blow, sound, trumpeter.
2691: (masculine and feminine); from חָצַר in its original sense; a yard (as inclosed by a fence); also a hamlet (as similarly surrounded with walls); court, tower, village.
2692: xlit Addâr corrected to ʼAddâr; from חָצֵר and אַדָּר; (the) village of Addar; Chatsar-Addar, a place in Palestine; Hazar-addar.
2693: from חָצֵר and a feminine of גַּד; (the) village of (female) Fortune; Chatsar-Gaddah, a place in Palestine; Hazar-gaddah.
2694: from חָצֵר and תִּיכוֹן with the article interposed; village of the middle; Chatsar-hat-Tikon, a place in Palestine; Hazar-hatticon.
2695: by an orthographical variation for חֶצְרוֹן; enclosure; Chetsro, an Israelite; Hezro, Hezrai.
2696: from חָצֵר; court-yard; Chetsron, the name of a place in Palestine; also of two Israelites; Hezron.
2697: patronymically from חֶצְרוֹן; a Chetsronite or (collectively) descendants of Chetsron; Hezronites.
2698: feminine plural of חָצֵר; yards; Chatseroth, a place in Palestine; Hazeroth.
2699: plural masculine of חָצֵר; yards; Chatserim, a place in Palestine; Hazerim.
